Adding initial findings from a quick run against the trace:
- The trace shows continuous inbound requests; our serving runtime emits chunks for the first ~180–220 tokens as expected.
- After approximately 220 tokens the server continues producing tokens, but we observe TCP-level idle timeouts on the client side in multiple traces. That suggests partial-frame delivery (some frames smaller than expected) leading to prolonged flush delays at the OS/socket layer.
- We see 502s in a minority of cases when an intermediary (some customer-side proxy) interprets the silence as a backend failure.

Immediate mitigations to try:
- Server-side: force periodic keepalive frames (every 3s) for the next 8 hours to prevent client-side proxies from closing.
- Client-side: recommend disabling strict proxy idle timeout for streams or increase it to 30s.

I attached a filtered runtime log that highlights the token emission windows. (attachment: acme-live-trace-20270326.log). I'm opening SUP-3421 to track.

Rishi
